requirements.evidence: All contract pieces are present: migrations for totems/totem_presets/totem_preset_queue (composite PK), models with entity()/queues() using preset_id/queue_id, Entity::totems()/totemPresets(), factories, `#[Signature('totem:pairing-code {preset}')]` with random_int + sprintf('%06d') and FAILURE on unknown preset, POST api/totem/auth with 400/401/200 + entity pair and lockForUpdate in DB::transaction (TotemAuthController.php:31-85), HS256 JWT with totem_id/entity_id/preset_id/queues/iat/exp/jti, totem.auth middleware with live array_intersect scope (TotemAuth.php:101-107), queues/priorities/ticket endpoints with 403/404/422 codes, IssueTicket with TicketChannel::Totem, throttle:10 and throttle:30, 429 rate_limited renderer in bootstrap/app.php, CORS, .env.example, phpunit.xml secret, docs updated. Small gaps: queue visual color/icon are hardcoded ('#0055FF','ticket', TotemController.php:158) and description is taken from an assumed labels_i18n key; totems.name is made nullable although the spec lists it as a plain column (create_totems_table.php:17).

conventions.evidence: Ticket issuance goes through App\Actions\IssueTicket (TotemController.php:91); $fillable set deliberately via #[Fillable]; migrations have reversible down(); CHANGELOG [Unreleased], docs/api/totem.md, docs/architecture.md and docs/database-schema.md updated. Deviations: input is validated with hand-rolled checks instead of $request->validate (justified by the custom error codes, but not the project pattern); scope checks are done in the controller rather than through a policy/gate; TotemJwtException is declared in app/Support/TotemJwt.php:99, which breaks PSR-4 one-class-per-file.

security.evidence: JWT signature is compared with hash_equals and alg is checked (TotemJwt.php:58-67); exp, totem/preset is_active and entity match between claims, totem and preset are enforced (TotemAuth.php:66-99); queues are resolved within the token entity only, so the effective scope is enforced; pairing uses the same 401 for every failure (no oracle) and the code is never logged; CORS has no credentials and the origin regex is anchored. Limited gaps: the ticket throttle is keyed by IP only (unauthenticated in Laravel's sense), so totems behind one NAT share a budget; there is no minimum secret length or startup check (an empty secret makes pairing throw a 500 via InvalidArgumentException).

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/TotemApiTest.php covers the artisan command (success, unknown preset), 400 formats including empty, 401 for unknown/expired/consumed/inactive, a successful pair with JWT claims and single use, the queue scope claim, the 429 pairing and ticket throttles, missing/forged/expired tokens, deactivated totem/preset, last_seen_at, queue listing order/visual.order/entity mismatch 403, immediate scope removal, priorities 404/403/422, sequential A001/A002 with channel totem, invalid priority, inactive queue, CORS allowed and denied origins, and the failure audit log without the code. Missing: a tamper test for entity mismatch between claims, totem and preset (e.g. a token signed with another entity's totem), the success audit log, and an assertion that the artisan command prints the code and writes an audit entry.

simplicity.evidence: The approach is direct and reuses IssueTicket; TotemPriorities is the single source for the endpoint and for validation; the small JWT class is allowed by the task. Some redundancy: the origin allow-list is defined twice (config/cors.php allowed_origins_patterns and TotemCors::isAllowedOrigin, with web_origin read from both env and services config); TotemPriorities::values() duplicates the data and is unused; TotemController::tokenEntity re-queries the Entity even though the middleware already resolved the totem/preset; the transaction closure returns an 'ok' array that adds indirection.

readability.evidence: Classes and methods are small and documented with PHPDoc (TotemAuth, TotemCors, TotemController::resolveQueue). Nits: a dead TotemPriorities::values() method; the default totem name 'Totem '.$preset->name produces 'Totem Totem ...' with factory data (TotemAuthController.php:54); there is no blank line between the last two tests (TotemApiTest.php:418-419); a second class lives in TotemJwt.php.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: models, migrations, factories, command, controllers, middleware, config, routes/api.php registration, throttle rendering, CORS, docs, CHANGELOG and tests. TotemCors is extra code, but it is there to meet the required 204 response to a bare preflight. No unrelated refactors.

issues.explanation: TotemJwtException is declared in TotemJwt.php instead of its own file, which breaks PSR-4 autoloading; it works only because TotemJwt is always loaded first.

The queue visual color/icon are hardcoded constants, and description reads an assumed labels_i18n['description'] key that is not shown in the diff, so the per-queue presentation is not really backend-driven.
There is no tamper test for an entity mismatch between JWT claims, totem and preset, and no test for the success audit log or for the command's printed code and audit entry.
The allowed-origin logic duplicates config/cors.php (the same regex, plus TOTEM_WEB_ORIGIN read through two different config paths), so the two can drift.
The ticket throttle has no authenticated user, so it is keyed by IP only; several totems behind one NAT share the 30/min budget, and limits are not per device.
totems.name is nullable although the data model lists it as a regular column.
values() is unused and duplicates the values already in all().
The default totem name 'Totem '.$preset->name produces redundant names such as 'Totem Totem foo'.
The last two test blocks have no blank line between them, unlike the rest of the file.

review.summary: The change implements the full totem BFF: migrations and models, the pairing artisan command, transactional pairing login with an HS256 JWT, the totem.auth middleware with live scope intersection, the three endpoints with issuance through IssueTicket, throttling with the rate_limited JSON, localhost CORS, docs, CHANGELOG and a broad feature test suite. The remaining issues are minor: a PSR-4 violation for the exception class, hardcoded queue visuals, duplicated CORS origin logic, and a few missing tamper and audit-log tests. Approve with small follow-ups.
